claim: Renewal price tests on digital-only news subscribers (not students, not software): about -0.05, i.e. 0.5% of subscribers stop per 10% price rise. A consultancy's result from its own clients' data.
quote: we found the price elasticity of these digital-only subscribers was approximately -.05

claim: Same source: engaged readers were about a quarter as price-sensitive as non-engaged ones.
quote: had price elasticity that was one-quarter the level of non-engaged digital subscribers

claim: A blog on iOS subscription apps says there is no single elasticity: acquisition and renewal respond differently.
quote: Subscription price elasticity is not a single number

claim: The same blog, citing RevenueCat and Sensor Tower, lists categories that are less price-sensitive when acquiring customers, education among them.
quote: Productivity and utilities, health and fitness, professional tools, education

claim: The same blog's own caveat on its evidence.
quote: That makes the evidence directional rather than causal
